newsitem.title: USA: Toys 'R' Us reports earnings jump.
newsitem.headline: Toys 'R' Us reports earnings jump.

text.p: Toys 'R' Us, the world's largest toy chain, reported a nearly 60 percent rise in third-quarter profits Monday, attributing the jump to a resurgence in sales of video game hardware and strong sales of dolls and other products.
The Paramus, N.J., company said its net earnings rose for the quarter ended Nov. 2 rose to $33 million, or 12 cents a share, from $21 million, or 8 cents a share.
Wall Street had expected profits of 11 cents a share, according to First Call, which tracks analyst forecasts.
The company said sales for the quarter rose 10 percent to $1.9 billion from $1.7 billion a year ago.
Toys 'R' Us stock rose 50 cents to $35.50 in late morning trading on the New York Stock Exchange.
Chief Executive Officer Michael Goldstein said in a statement that for the third consecutive quarter all the company's divisions reported increases in sales at stores open for at least a year.

Goldstein said U.S. sales were driven by the resurgence of video game hardware sales prompted by the release of Nintendo Co. Ltd.'s Nintendo 64 video game machine Sept. 29 "as well as strong sales of basic toy products such as dolls and action figures."
Sales were also strong in Canada, Britain and Japan, he said.
